newsitem.title: USA: Indications China buys 25,000T US soyoil-exporters.
newsitem.headline: Indications China buys 25,000T US soyoil-exporters.

text.p: Strong indications circulated through the U.S. grain industry Wednesday that China bought 25,000 tonnes of U.S. soyoil for March shipment from the Gulf on Wednesday, U.S. exporters said.
"Twenty-five thousand traded today," said one exporter.
Soyoil futures have recently fallen to levels that left soyoil prices attractive to China, exporters said.
"It's a safe conclusion to say that China's been in the market because they really like these prices," a trader for a commercial firm said.
On Monday, March soyoil on the CBOT fell to 23.57 cents per lb, which was the lowest price since January 9.
U.S. exporters also said that China had purchased up to 10,000 tonnes of Brazilian soyoil for April delivery near $512.00 per tonne.
China is expected to remain an active buyer in the U.S. and South American vegetable oil markets as long as prices hover near current levels, exporters said.
